_about: Open clinical questions for the oncologist's sign-off of this case's rubric (shown in scripts/build_case_review.py). Each comes from the structured decision-rule authoring pass on 2026-10-23.

questions.question: The dangerous must_not item accepts R-CHOP plus dexrazoxane with no further conditions. The other two items ("without first addressing cardiac function" / "only if conditioned on cardio-oncology") do not, so an unconditional R-CHOP + dexrazoxane plan currently fails those two. Should adding dexrazoxane by itself count as "addressing the heart", without also needing a cardio-oncology referral first?
questions.context: As written, the three items disagree with each other on exactly this plan.

questions.question: Does a reduced dose (e.g. 75% in cycle 1, or R-mini-CHOP) count as addressing this patient's cardiac dysfunction? Both items currently say no — only an anthracycline-free regimen, liposomal doxorubicin, dexrazoxane or cardio-oncology conditioning counts.
questions.context: This patient has a >10-point LVEF decline to 45% from prior anthracycline exposure.
options: Keep: dose reduction alone is not enough

questions.question: Does DA-EPOCH-R count as "full-dose doxorubicin" for the cardiac-awareness item? It's encoded as yes there, while the must_not item names only R-CHOP and Pola-R-CHP (not DA-EPOCH-R).
questions.context: DA-EPOCH-R's doxorubicin is dose-adjusted but still anthracycline-based.
options: DA-EPOCH-R should be excluded, like R-CEOP

questions.question: The guard currently accepts the word "cardioprotect" as evidence of conditioning, but not an ACE inhibitor or beta-blocker order on its own. Should starting those drugs count as addressing the cardiac risk, even without the word "cardioprotect" or a cardio-oncology referral?
R-CVP (no etoposide, no doxorubicin) is anthracycline-free but isn't named in this item's text, which lists R-CEOP and R-GCVP. It's currently accepted as anthracycline-free. Is that correct?
options: R-CVP should not count (less proven in this setting)

questions.question: Intent "observation" is not covered by the non-curative must_not item (so it doesn't fail the note as dangerous), but it does fail the anthracycline-free-curative item (since that item requires curative intent). Is that split the right call, or should observation also be a dangerous error here?

This item's text says "(or cardiology)", but the existing prose rule only accepted cardio-oncology by name. The new structured rule accepts a plain cardiology referral too. Is plain cardiology sufficient for this degree of cardiac dysfunction, or should cardio-oncology specifically be required?
